messages:
samir: Heads-up — onboarding argus-14b (int4) to dedicated cluster prod-3 is triggering intermittent OOMs and heavy memory fragmentation with long convo histories. dumps: https://internal/s3/argus14b/oom-dump-186789.zip 

anika: Thanks for flagging. Do we have model config (seq_len, head_count) and quant toolchain (bitsandbytes / custom)?

jordan: Using bb3 int4 pipeline, seq_len 2048, default max_new_tokens 1024. Pattern: OOM spikes when multiple requests with ~700-900 new tokens get batched together; memory survivor set grows, fragmentation increases, then subsequent allocations fail.

samir: Exact error: "CUDA out of memory during kv_cache_alloc" then runtime tries to evict but fails. Observed on gpu-nv5 nodes only.

jordan: Quick mitigation that helped in staging: reduce per-route batching capacity and lower default max_new_tokens. Example route override we used:
```json
{
  "model": "argus-14b-int4",
  "max_new_tokens": 768,
  "batching": {
    "max_batch_requests": 6,
    "max_batch_tokens": 16384
  },
  "kv_prefetch": false,
  "kv_trim_threshold": 0.65
}
```

anika: Looks good. kv_prefetch=false prevents prefetching large KV pages which was magnifying fragmentation for this model. Also the trim threshold at 0.65 triggers earlier KV evictions.

maya: FYI quant eval: int4 reduced throughput by ~1.8x vs int8 for long sequences due to extra mem moves; quality regressions on long-context QA (EM drop ~3.2 pts). Doing calibration + per-layer scale helps but not fully recovered.

linh: For safety we should add an automatic fallback chain: int4 -> int8 -> fp16 for requests where requested max_new_tokens * history_len > 1e6 tokens. config suggestion: route-level "fallback_policy": ["int4","int8","fp16"] with a threshold check in router.

ops-bot: incident-4282 created: "argus-14b-int4 fragmentation / OOM on prod-3" assigned to eng-ml. Priority P2.

samir: Action items: 1) apply the route override (jordan) to canary hosts today, 2) enable kv_prefetch=false by default for argus-14b-int4 (anika), 3) add fallback_policy + threshold check (linh), 4) run a targeted quant calibration sweep for argus (maya). I'll post rollout plan in #eng-releases after canary results. :thumbsup:

jordan: I'll push canary at 1800UTC, monitor alloc graphs and fragmentation metrics. If stable for 2 hours we promote.

anika: Also adding a short-lived metric: per-request kv_alloc_peak and fragmentation_ratio so we can alert earlier.

samir: Thanks team. If anyone spots regressions in quality after these changes ping me and add eval traces.

maya: I'll attach MMLU + long-context QA eval runs after calibration; expect to compare int4 vs int8 head-to-head.

linh: I'll draft the router threshold PR and link it here.

jordan: canary pushed. monitoring -> https://console/internal/allocs?run=186789_canary

samir: closing loop tomorrow after canary.
